To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the adaptive wavelet scheme for stochastic partial differential equations converges with optimal order and that the tolerances for the adaptive scheme have to be chosen appropriately.

the inexact implicit Euler scheme is stable and converges with optimal order if the tolerances in each time step are chosen appropriately, that this can be achieved by a suitable adaptive wavelet or adaptive finite-element discretization, and that this leads to a fully adaptive numerical method that is guaranteed to converge with the same rate of convergence as the exact implicit Euler scheme.

(i) for the linearly implicit Euler scheme, the convergence order of the Rothe discretization is the same as for the fully implicit Euler scheme and that (ii) the adaptive wavelet method is able to realize the optimal convergence order of the discretization scheme.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the convergence analysis of an inexact linearly implicit Euler scheme applied to a class of semilinear stochastic evolution equations.
the analysis and design of adaptive schemes for the efficient numerical treatment of stochastic PDEs.
the analysis of adaptive numerical schemes for stochastic partial differential equations and with the development of efficient algorithms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the inexact linearly implicit Euler scheme is a robust and efficient method for solving SPDEs.

adaptive Rothe’s methods are a viable option for the efficient and reliable solution of SPDEs, and that they are robust in terms of the order of convergence and in the sense that they can handle the full range of the involved parameters.
the Rothe scheme with the proposed adaptive spatial discretization realizes the optimal order of convergence, if the time discretization step is chosen appropriately.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
adaptive wavelet or Galerkin methods for stochastic elliptic problems are feasible for the time discretizations by Rothe’s method.
we show how to adaptively solve a class of stochastic partial differential equation with optimal order of convergence.
we show how to combine the adaptive discretization schemes with the implicit Euler method such that the overall convergence order is not affected by the inexact evaluations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the tolerances have a different dependence on the time step than the one that is commonly assumed.
, under certain mild assumptions on the spatial adaptive scheme, the order of convergence is preserved.
the adaptive wavelet method is a viable candidate for the adaptive numerical treatment in stochastic partial differential equations.
